transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, what brings me in today is... I keep hearing these very clear voices. It happens mostly in my apartment, but sometimes when I'm out, too, like in empty museum rooms. 

It sounds exactly like women whispering from right behind the walls. They keep telling me which photographs belong in the archive. It's just so clear and it's been happening a lot, so I figured I needed to come in and talk to someone about it.
How long have you been hearing these voices?
Well, the voices... and this feeling I have that people are watching my archive, it's all been going on for about eight months now.
Aside from the voices and the feeling of being watched, have you noticed any significant changes in your memory or your ability to focus on daily tasks?

Well, yes, my focus has definitely changed. It's been very hard to concentrate lately. If I try to read a letter or... or even just sit and talk with my cousin, I can't seem to stay on track. 

Something small, like a siren outside, the hum of the refrigerator, or just a certain color in a brochure sitting on the table—it just pulls me away completely. I lose the thread of what I was doing or saying almost immediately.
Have you experienced any significant head injuries, seizures, or been diagnosed with any serious medical conditions recently?

No, I haven't. I've never had any head injuries or seizures, and I haven't been diagnosed with any medical conditions like that. Physically, I'm perfectly fine. It's just... the voices and the trouble focusing.
When you have these conversations with your cousin, do they ever tell you that what you are saying doesn't make sense or that you are jumping between unrelated topics?

Yes, actually, she does say that. It happens a lot lately. She'll ask me something simple, like... maybe about a bill, or an upcoming appointment. And I'll try to answer, but I end up talking about the grant I'm working on, and then somehow that leads into the shipping routes, and then... well, then I'm talking about my grandmother's altar. By the time I finish explaining it all, she just looks confused, and nobody really knows what I originally meant to say. I don't mean to do it, it just all connects in my head at the time.
Do you find that you have less interest in socializing or doing things you used to enjoy, or that it's become harder to express your emotions or keep up a conversation?

Yes, I suppose I have. There are... well, there are long stretches where I just sit at my kitchen table. I used to take care of these herb pots, but lately, I just let them dry out. I don't really have the energy for it. 

And socializing... I haven't been calling my friends back. Even when someone invites me out to something I used to like, you know, like a concert or a gallery opening, I just don't feel much interest in going. It just feels too hard to keep up a conversation or really feel anything about it.
Have you noticed any times where your body becomes completely rigid, or conversely, where you find yourself unable to move or speak for long periods of time?

I don't think I get completely rigid or unable to speak, no. But I do get stuck doing certain things or holding certain positions sometimes. 

Like... well, I was at this postponed museum program recently, and I just felt compelled to arrange all the chairs into a kind of island map. And after I did that, I went up to the front of the room and just stood there with my arms lifted up. I couldn't just walk away or put my arms down, because leaving felt like I was disobeying the message I had been given. So I just stayed standing like that for a while.
Have you experienced any distinct periods in these past eight months where your mood was extremely high or low, lasting for a week or more?

Yes, I do have times like that. There will be a week or so where my mood is very high and I just feel... radiant. I get these days when I feel like I have been chosen. 

But it can turn. If someone questions my plan during those times, or if they tell me I need to slow down, I become absolutely furious. It feels as if they are trying to erase me.

During those weeks when your mood was extremely high or low, were you still hearing the voices and feeling like people were watching your archive, or did those experiences stop during those specific periods?

Yes, they were still there. Even during the periods when my mood was very high and I was sleeping only a few hours... when I was just racing from one archive task to another, I was still hearing the women’s voices. And I still felt absolutely certain that the museum board was tracking my work. So, no, they didn't stop during those times.

Looking back over the entire eight-month period, would you say that you spent more of that time feeling that 'radiant' high mood, or were those periods relatively short compared to the times you felt more low or neutral?

Well, looking back... I'd say the high moods have definitely taken up the majority of the time. 

Since I retired eight months ago, most of that time has been dominated by those stretches where I feel so driven and chosen, like I mentioned. Even when I have a few quieter days where I just withdraw, those periods of feeling so radiant—and so irritable if people get in my way—and just completely unable to slow down... those have definitely been the main part of these past months.
